pattern: Single-line API re-exports that forward to another package function without adding logic, validation, or transformation
decision: These wrappers consolidate dispatch-related concerns under the dispatch package API. Callers use dispatch for Cast/Resolve; having dispatch expose WorktreePath and NewSessionManager avoids requiring callers to import internal/config or internal/session for what are conceptually dispatch operations. Thin re-exports in an internal package are a defensible API boundary choice, not OVERBUILD.

pattern: Comments saying 'ported from internal/adapter/X' or 'descriptor fields ported from internal/adapter/X/X.go' where the source package was deleted
decision: 'Ported from X' is historical provenance documentation, not an active assertion that X still exists. Contrast with a survival clause ('preserved until W5') which actively asserts the source is still present and is correctly flagged (CF-01, S1). Port-provenance comments are standard Go practice for describing code lineage; flagging them as MISLEAD conflates a stale file-path reference with an actively misleading claim. The fd2db8e commit deliberately retained this framing while fixing an actual error, confirming it is an intentional documentation style.

pattern: Mixed typed (*Var) and anonymous (GetBool/GetString) flag binding styles across commands within the same file, where each individual command is internally consistent
decision: cmd/CONVENTIONS.md Section 2 permits both flag-binding forms and mandates only per-command consistency ('Within a single command, don't mix the two forms'). Each command satisfies this rule, so the file-level mix is not a convention violation. NOTE: cmd/writ.go has a distinct, real violation (CF-27) where individual commands mix both forms within one command — that is NOT covered by this exemption and should be fixed.

pattern: Core test runner helpers (runGT, gtBin, projectRoot) defined in cli_test.go rather than helpers_test.go
decision: runGT and gtBin are co-located with the binary build target (gtBin) they depend on — a defensible home. Moving them to helpers_test.go is a preferred-style reorganization, not a correction. Fails the stable-target gate (just 'more organized', not clearly better) and does not actively mislead about coverage, defeat an isolation rule, or exhibit fixture drift.

pattern: Two near-duplicate test environment setup functions with an underdocumented behavioral distinction (gitRun vs runGit helper, initial.txt vs README.md)
decision: The two functions are genuinely distinct tools for different test contexts (different git-env-var behavior, different initial file layout) — not accidental duplicates that will drift. The orientation cost of the underdocumented distinction is minor (seconds to compare two short functions). Does not meet the test-specific bar: no misleading about coverage, no defeated isolation rule, no drifted fixture. Revisit if the two functions ever begin to diverge in a way that risks silent drift.
